subject: Proposal: term refactor + retention credit to support capacity uplift
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-19T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: BrightCart — usage jump + proposal for term refactor and retention credit

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the time yesterday. I pulled together a short recap of what we saw in Q2 and a proposal for how Redwood can help BrightCart scale without immediate headroom risk. Attaching the Q2 usage report.

Quick summary:
- Token spend doubled month-over-month in April→May, driven by the new checkout personalization microservice (avg seq len 450).
- Current Dedicated tier is maxed during PST peak 11:00–14:00 with tail latency increases; cost per 1k tokens spiked due to repeated cold starts on larger sequences.
- BrightCart is approaching renewal (contract ends 2028-07-31).

Proposal (high level):
1) Term refactor: move from 12-month fixed commitment to a 9-month staggered term with built-in headroom buffer for Q3 traffic spikes.
2) Retention credit: one-time credit applied to July invoice to smooth migration to the new term (value proposed: $25k).
3) Capacity uplift: temporary burst pool for peak window and autoscale tuning to reduce cold-starts and per-token price volatility.

If this works for you I’ll draft a mutual action plan and loop in Ben + Laura to align on pricing and legal. Can you confirm procurement contact and any internal timeline constraints?

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: BrightCart_Q2_usage_report.pdf (summary + perf graphs)

From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@brightcart.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-19T11:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightCart — usage jump + proposal for term refactor and retention credit

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the proactive summary and the numbers. A few clarifying Qs from our side:

1) Can you quantify the expected latency improvement with the proposed burst pool + autoscale tweaks? We need a concrete SLO before we talk to engineering.
2) For the retention credit, does that reduce committed spend or is it a one-off billing credit? Procurement prefers credits that don't change committed baseline.
3) Procurement contact is procurement@brightcart.com (cc'd on this reply). We have a board review scheduled on 2028-06-13 and would like final commercial terms by 2028-06-07 to make the packet.

Also looping in our Ops lead (cc). Can you share a short mutual action plan (MAP) that shows timeline + deliverables?

Best,
Sarah Lim
Head of Platform
BrightCart

(On Fri, May 19, 2028 at 09:14, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@brightcart.com>, BrightCart Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-20T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: BrightCart — usage jump + proposal for term refactor and retention credit

Hi Sarah — thanks, and noted on your timelines. Short answers:

1) Latency: with the burst pool + aggressive KV prefix caching we expect 95th percentile generation latency to drop ~30–45% for the affected endpoints (from ~900ms down to ~500–600ms) based on similar workloads we ran during the Dedicated pilot. I'll include the perf trace examples in the MAP.
2) Retention credit: proposed as a one-time invoice credit (does not reduce your committed baseline). It is intended to smooth the billing impact during transition.
3) Timeline: I'll attach a 3-week MAP that lines up with your board packet deadline.

Attached: MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_BrightCart.xlsx, term_refactor_summary.pdf

Next steps:
- I will prepare a commercial term sheet with the $25k credit and the 9-month staggered term options for internal review.
- Ben, Laura — can you confirm if $25k credit is approvable from our side under the current deal authority, and whether legal needs any special language for the term refactor?

Sarah — if we can get a verbal OK on the $25k and the timeline, I can turn around the DocuSign link by end of day tomorrow.

Thanks,
Karthik

Attachment: MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_BrightCart.xlsx (timeline + owners), term_refactor_summary.pdf

---

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-20T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightCart — usage jump + proposal for term refactor and retention credit

Karthik — quick internal note. I reviewed the proposed $25k retention credit against current quota approvals. We have two levers: (A) approve $25k as a one-time credit within existing AE discount budget, or (B) convert part of that into a temporary burst credit (non-billable) applied via a usage cap waiver for 60 days. Option B preserves cashflow better for Redwood.

Legal (Laura) — any objections to (B)? We'll need a short addendum that calls out the burst pool duration and the non-recurring nature of the waiver. Also confirm if this requires CFO pre-approval.

If all good, we can offer Sarah a blended approach: $15k invoice credit + 60-day burst waiver to cover the immediate peak. That reduces Redwood exposure and helps Procurement sign faster.

Ben
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-20T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightCart — usage jump + proposal for term refactor and retention credit

Ben / Karthik — I spoke with Legal and Finance. Short: (B) is OK with the following additions to the addendum:
- Explicit burst pool start/end dates (we suggest 2028-06-01 → 2028-07-30).
- Performance guardrails (max hourly qps and fallback model) to limit risk.
- Invoice credit of $15,000 applied to July invoice, plus the 60-day burst waiver as a non-recurring concession.

Finance requests the deal desk sign-off; I can slot this for approval today if you provide the final numbers and the MAP. Karthik — please confirm the exact list of endpoints we are covering (checkout personalization only, or also search-responder). Also confirm that MAP has the perf traces Sarah requested.

Laura
VP Legal & Finance (acting)
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@brightcart.com>, BrightCart Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-22T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Final commercial outline & next steps (MAP + DocuSign)

Sarah / Procurement — thanks for the fast turnaround and the heads-up on the board packet date. Per internal approvals, Redwood can offer the blended package below:

Commercial outline (agreed in principle):
- Term refactor: new 9-month staggered term starting 2028-06-01, terminating 2029-02-28.
- Credit & burst: $15,000 invoice credit applied to July 2028 invoice + 60-day burst pool (2028-06-01→2028-07-30) with defined guardrails.
- Capacity: immediate autoscale tuning and prefix KV caching applied to checkout personalization endpoints (we will include search-responder only if BrightCart confirms before 2028-05-25).
- Acceptance: performance SLO target — 95th percentile latency <= 650ms for covered endpoints during peak hours.

Deliverables & dates (MAP attached):
- 2028-05-23: DocuSign term addendum (I will send link today).
- 2028-05-24 → 2028-05-31: Engineering runbook implementation & perf validation.
- 2028-06-01: Burst pool live.

DocuSign link: https://app.redwood.example/docusign/BRIGHT-2028-01
Attachments: MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_BrightCart.xlsx, term_refactor_summary.pdf

Please reply with a confirmation of the procurement contact and a green light on the July credit. If I don't hear back by 2028-05-24 EOD PT I will follow up by phone.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_BrightCart.xlsx, BrightCart_Q2_usage_report.pdf, term_refactor_summary.pdf
